rows.title: Champion rules (d12)
rows.body_md:
# Champion rules (d12)

When **Champion rules** are on, the floor runs **d12 roll-under** Twilight Sword maths. You are a **Champion** in service of **the Scourge** — eight stats, hearts, and roll-under on the die.

The phone and handbook stay the same places; labels and maths change. This page is the player cheat sheet. The app also exports code-synced detail under **Rules → Champion rolls** and **Combat house rules**.

## The die

Roll **d12**. **Lower is better** — you succeed when the final die result is **less than or equal to** the relevant ability score.

- **Bonuses help** by **subtracting** from the die (easier to roll low).
- **Penalties hurt** by **adding** to the die.
- Circumstance mods on one roll **cap at ±3** after advantage is resolved.
- **Natural 1** = critical success (attacks can crit for champions only).
- **Natural 12** = critical failure (setback — fumbles, broken gear, and similar).

**Advantage:** roll **2d12, keep the lower**. **Disadvantage:** **2d12, keep the higher**. They cancel to a single level — never stack extra dice beyond one adv/dis pair.

## The eight stats

| Code | Name | Replaces (legacy) |
|------|------|-------------------|
| STR | Strength | STR |
| AGL | Agility | DEX |
| VIT | Vitality | CON |
| PER | Perception | (new) |
| WIL | Will | WIS |
| KNO | Knowledge | INT |
| CHA | Charisma | CHA |
| STE | Stealth | (new) |

On the Me shelf you see all eight when Champion rules are on; legacy nights still show the old five-stat strip.

## Hearts, stamina, armour

- **Hearts** replace hit points: **max hearts = 10 + VIT** (plus permanent heartstones).
- Incoming damage subtracts **armour rating** first, then hearts.
- At **0 hearts** you make a **WIL** roll-under on your turn — success **hangs on** and keep acting at 0; fail = **K.O.** Drop far below 0 and auto K.O. checks apply in the app.
- **Stamina** starts at **3** (default cap **3** unless stones say otherwise). Spend **1** to: take advantage on a roll, activate a feat, recast an expended spell, or burn a scroll without a check.
- **Boon** (rare): one champion per evening may hold a boon — spend for a forced crit success, a dramatic save, or full stamina recovery (see Me tab when live).

## Words at the table

- **Champions** — player characters.
- **The Scourge** — the floor’s big evil; lore may call foes heartless.
- **Hearts** — your wound track (shown as ♥ on the phone when rules are on).

## Combat flow

**Initiative:** d12 roll-under — **lowest goes first**. Ambush gives advantage; being ambushed gives disadvantage on that roll.

**Your attack:** melee uses **STR** (or **AGL** on finesse weapons); ranged uses **PER**. No target number — beat your own stat on the d12. On a hit, roll weapon damage; **nat 1** on the attack roll can **double damage** (champions only — monsters never crit).

**Monster attacks:** hostiles usually skip an attack roll — they declare a target and roll **damage only**. After you see that damage, you may use your **one reaction this round**:

- **Dodge** — **AGL** roll-under; success means no hearts lost.
- **Parry** — **STR** roll-under with a **melee weapon or shield** in hand; no parrying ranged shots unless you have a shield.

The phone shows a dodge/parry banner when that window is open.

**Ranges:** Close · Near · Far (and **too far** when you are out of the fight but can still support). Ranged attacks suffer disadvantage at **close**. Leaving melee may need an **AGL** disengage check.

**Actions:** one main action per turn plus free swaps in your **equipped pool** (three slots — heavy weapons use two). Fetching from the backpack costs your turn.

## Rest

**Solo rest** in a safe room still costs rations and downtime, but recovery under Champion rules heals **d12 hearts**, restores **+1 stamina**, and offers a **pick-one** bonus (extra hearts, extra stamina, clear a status, or recharge a spell). Party camp uses the same champion rest pass when the flag is on.

_Edit this file, then run `uv run python -m dnd wiki export` to refresh the public site._

rows.body_md:
# Running the table (DM)

The **DM UI** is the browser on the Mac at **port 8766** — loopback only. Players use **8767** on their phones. Voice chat is for talk; every game action happens in one of those two sites.

This page is a short cheat sheet for tonight’s tools. Full DM UI architecture lives in the private app repo (`docs/DM_UI.md`).

## Who is online

Connected champions get a **green dot** on their portrait in the party strip, on room PC cards, and on the combat initiative row. If the dot is missing, that player’s phone has not heartbeated in a while.

## PC sheet

Click a champion in the party strip or combat roster.

- **Statuses** paint on the **backdrop** behind the sheet (not inside the card). Each chip shows **what caused it** when the app knows.
- **Clear all statuses** sits on that backdrop row — one button clears every affliction on that PC.
- **HP** pills are sized to the digits; in **combat**, use the HP pad on party or lane rows for typed damage and healing.
- **Gear** uses the shared paper doll; **Spells / Active / Passive** are three columns.
- **Hostage** replaced the old backpack strip on the Me tab — at most **one** packed person or obstacle per champion (see the player guide).
- A champion **resting alone** on their phone shows **💤** on the sheet; **Wake now** ends sleep early (`pc_wake_rest`).

## Combat console

Turn order is a wide sidebar with per-row actions, a room drawer, **Next turn**, and optional auto-attack. Clicking an NPC portrait opens the NPC sheet again.

After a fight, the board paint returns to explore mode without leaving stale combat chrome.

## DM room (summoned room)

The free-look column’s summoned room gets the same treatment as a normal room: **+** to stage things, **room menu** for effects, and **move PCs** in and out. Re-stage offstage catalog pieces once per visit; never duplicate a node already on the board.

## Kitchen Stadium / cook-off

When a cook-show is running and PCs are in Kitchen Stadium:

- The **cook-off panel** shows phase, crew, shelves, locks, checks, and scores.
- **Start cook-off** (DM button) moves every active PC to Kitchen Stadium and begins the show on every client — same as the signpost **enter** on phones.

Players also get a **Kitchen Stadium** bottom tab for the duration; they can browse away and tap it to return.

## Party rest vs solo rest

**Party rest** still runs from the DM (**camp** intent) and heals everyone with the usual interruption d6.

Each champion may also **rest alone** from their phone in a safe room (two food units, downtime, then a timed sleep). You can **Wake now** from their sheet if the table needs them moving.

## Quick checks

| Situation | Where to look |
|-----------|----------------|
| Mystery gold on a deed | Deed now names a **source** slug in the log and on the phone |
| Corpse loot | App rolls **50% pocket change** or **50% Bronze Loot Box**, not both (regular monsters) |
| Optional late checks | Search/social DCs on “optional” spots are tuned to about **DC 12**, not unfair 17s |
| Bleacher Tunnel | Room **328** is **dark** until someone holds a real light (e.g. Pitch Torch) |

_For deep architecture and intent keys, ask Pete or open `docs/DM_UI.md` in the app checkout._

rows.title: Glossary
rows.body_md:
# Glossary

Short names for things you will see on the player app and in session.

## Champion

Your player character when **Champion rules (d12)** are on — the app still calls you a **champion** in data, but the handbook uses Champion for hearts, stamina, and roll-under.

## The Scourge

Floor Three’s overarching evil in champion flavour — heartless monsters, big set-piece villains, and lore that treats the party as Champions holding the line.

## Hearts

Your wound track under Champion rules (**10 + VIT** max, plus heartstones). The phone shows ♥ instead of HP when the flag is on.

## Equipped pool

Three combat-ready slots (weapons, shield, potions) under Champion rules. Swapping within the pool is free; fetching from the backpack costs your turn.

## Champion

Your PC on Floor Three — level, gear, deeds, and lore all hang off this identity.

## Deed

Something the table logged that counts toward achievements, sponsor taste, and evening scoring. You do not edit deeds on the wiki; they sync from play.

## Achievement wall

Trophy cards with hints. Progress shows on your phone first; the wiki exports **hints and tallies**, not the secret “for” text.

## Board bounty

A name from the **top ten** on the world leaderboard. Each session start the app rolls whether one of those names is “on the floor” tonight. Posted gold is **150–500 gp** (tougher rivals toward the top of that band). When a floor quest pays for the capture or kill, it matches the posted amount — not the old thousands-scale poster copy.

## Sponsor / booth

Evening brands that court champions based on deeds. Invites and contracts stay in the app until you earn them.

## Rival kitchen

An NPC your table turned into a Stadium opponent. Rivals reset when the evening resets.

## AI Favour

A once-per-roll token that counts as **advantage** on that check. You can hold at most one.

## Peek / live

**Peek** restores the world when the DM stops the app. **Live** play can diverge from the wiki snapshot at any time.

## Quick slots

Three header slots for consumables and thrown gear you assign from the pack — usable in combat without opening the full inventory sheet.

## Library credit

Points earned from Kitchen Stadium cook-shows. Spend through **Info → Library** when the table has catalogue votes open.

## Hostage

At most one person or obstacle you are **dragging** in a dedicated slot on **Me**. Actions include shielding, trading back, executing, or harder diplomacy plays.

## Bearing

A mount’s extra **pack slot** for stashing items while you ride.

## Champion Cooler

Carrying this gear **pauses meat rotting** in your pack. Without it, meat and flesh spoil after about **90 minutes** of real time.

## Bleacher Tunnel

A **dark** service tunnel near the Stadium — bring a real light (torch, lantern) or searches suffer.

rows.body_md:
# House rules

This table runs **Twilight Sword** at the core, with Floor Three house conventions baked into the app. The published rulebook is not copied here — ask the DM or use the in-app **Library**.

**Champion rules (d12 roll-under):** when enabled on the campaign, player characters are **Champions**, foes serve **the Scourge**, and hearts/stamina/reactions replace the check_roll HP loop. Start with **[Champion rules (d12)](d12-champions)** — then the generated **Champion rolls**, **Combat house rules**, and **Phone combat** pages for numbers pulled from code.

**Auto-generated pages** (legacy check_roll rolls, party votes, effect tables, etc.) refresh on each `wiki export` — browse the Rules section in the handbook.

## Rolls at this table

**Legacy (flag off):**

- Stat and skill checks are usually a **flat check_roll** unless a status or armour too heavy for your STR imposes disadvantage.
- Weapon swings use a flat check_roll; a held weapon skill adds its rank to hit.
- Natural 1 on an attack: DC 12 DEX check or the weapon breaks. Guns, power tools and firebombs break outright.
- Spellcasting checks and saves stay flat check_roll.

**Champion rules (flag on):** d12 **roll-under** against ability scores; see **Champion rules (d12)**. Weapon feats and armour feats still unlock from play when the table uses them.

## The player app

- **Floor map** and **archive** only show what the party has already discovered in play.
- **Combat** on the phone is turn-gated; the server enforces what you can tap — greyed buttons are not a suggestion.
- **Travel** is per champion. Stepping into a room that would **start combat** asks for confirmation first. **Party votes** need a majority of champions present — **solo rest** is per champion, not a vote.
- **Info** uses a segment hub (Archive, Map, Library, Bonds, …). **Kitchen Stadium** tab applies during cook-offs as in **Using the player app**.
- **Champion rules on:** header shows **hearts** and **stamina**; combat may offer **dodge/parry** after foe damage; **equipped pool** replaces quick slots. **Flag off:** HP chip and quick slots behave as before.
- House pages **Supplies & statuses** and **Phone combat** list ammo, debuff clocks, meat spoilage, corpse loot, and search-fail ambushes the server enforces.

## Floor Three flavour

- Achievements on the wall are **hints**, not full quest write-ups.
- **Projects** and **bonds** are party-driven — see their Rules pages for payouts.

_Edit this file, then run `uv run python -m dnd wiki export` to refresh the public site._

rows.title: Loot boxes
rows.body_md:
# Loot boxes

Achievement payouts and some scenes award **bronze**, **silver**, or **gold** boxes. Opening a box rolls on the tier’s table in the adventure data — the wiki does not publish the full d100 lists (that would spoil the dungeon).

## Tiers (flavor)

- **Bronze** — Junk, scraps, and vending-machine surprises — still useful if you are clever.
- **Silver** — Better gear and potions from the silver table.
- **Gold** — Premium pulls — rare kit and strong potions.

## At the table

The player app shows what you rolled after the DM confirms the open. Exact items stay in your inventory and gear archive, not on this public site.

## Corpse search (monsters)

Searching a regular monster corpse (not a boss) rolls **50%** small pocket change **or** **50%** a **Bronze Loot Box** — never both. Bosses use the richer tier tables instead.

rows.title: Using the player app
rows.body_md:
# Using the player app

The **player app** is the site you open on your phone during session. Voice chat is for talking only — rolls, combat, inventory, and room text all happen here.

Layout: a **header** (portrait, vitals, statuses, stats, **quick slots** or **equipped pool**), the **room panel**, and bottom nav — **Home · Logs · Me · Notifications · Info · Settings**. During a cook-off you may also see **Kitchen Stadium** (🍳) until the show ends. With **[Champion rules (d12)](d12-champions)** on, the header shows **hearts** and **stamina** and three equipped slots instead of HP quick slots.

## The header

- **Portrait** — green ring while you hold **AI Favour**; tap to arm it for your next roll.
- **HP chip** — tap to adjust HP (table rules permitting).
- **Status chips** — icons only; long-press for cause and time left. **Follower** is 👤, **mount** is 🏇. A **Following** chip appears while you trail another champion; tap it to stop.
- **Quick slots** — three tappable slots for potions, thrown weapons, and other combat-ready consumables. Tap to use; long-press to assign from the pack. The **trinket** neck slot is only for real trinkets and magic jewellery — not every odd consumable.
- **Ability strip** — each stat shows **score and modifier**, e.g. `14 (+2)`. Tap a stat for a freeform check_roll that lands in the activity log.
- **Room mates** — when other champions share your room, their faces appear across the header; tap one for a read-only peek at their sheet.

**Plot clocks** sit under the header band (not over the room picture).

IMG|assets/guide/01-explore.png|Home — the room list on the left; Tess has a quest for you

## Home: the room panel

Between fights the room splits in two:

- **Left:** everyone and everything here — **people → obstacles → items** — with attitude, quest, and secret chips. Tap a row to act. **Long-press** an item (here or on the paper doll) to read it **without** unequipping. A **?** row is an unspotted secret; tap to search (failed party searches can eventually stir trouble — see **House rules → Supplies & statuses**). Someone with work for you lights in your colour with **QUEST** — tap for the offer; **Accept** or **Decline** (declined quests stay on that NPC with a **Read** option).
- **Right:** the **room picture** ( **Zone** / **Room** flips to the zone map), **Travel**, **Rest** / **Join combat** when they apply.

**Travel into a fight:** if the exit would start combat as soon as you step in, the app asks **Yes / No** on a bottom sheet before you move. **Go hostile** on someone in the room still starts a fight immediately.

IMG|assets/guide/02-travel.png|Travel — pick an exit; Gather and Follow sit below

## Moving, leading, and mounts

**Travel is per champion.** Pick an exit or tap a thumbnail on the zone map. **Gather** and **Follow** are in the travel sheet.

**Leading an NPC:** choose an exit that is actually open for you — sealed gates refuse with a clear message.

**Mount offers** do not spam after you refuse or already have a follower — new offers can include **swap** (ditch the current companion). A mount may carry a **bearing** slot for extra pack items. Riding a reluctant humanoid mount risks a bad mood once in a while when you change rooms.

## Solo rest

In a **safe room**, when you have enough food, a rest sheet can open (once per room visit on your phone). **Begin** spends **two** food units (rations, jerky, bread, or cooking ingredients — cheapest eaten first), runs a full personal recovery pass, lets you pick **downtime**, then sleeps **about ten minutes** while travel and other actions are blocked. Combat in your room wakes you — healing already applied. Party **votes** for end-night, retreat, surrender, and scout are unchanged; the old party-vote “rest everyone” bar is gone from the phone.

Fights replace the room panel: initiative strip, map, combat log, and your action menu. Use **quick slots** on your turn when you assigned them. See **Phone combat** in Rules for turn flow and **Solo flee** for leaving alone.

Some tunnels (e.g. **Bleacher Tunnel**) are **dark**. Without a held light source, searches and movement suffer; equip a torch or lantern in hand.

When you level, talent picks that add **+2 to one ability** apply to **that ability only** — not a second stat by mistake.

rows.body_md:
# Champion rolls (d12)

When **Champion rules** are enabled on the campaign, the table uses **d12 roll-under** — see the authored **[Champion rules (d12)](d12-champions)** page. When the flag is off, use **D12 rolls (house)** below.

d12 roll-under rules — leaf module for the Champion rules overhaul.

Bonus modifiers **subtract** from the die; penalties **add**. Success when the
adjusted die is ≤ the ability score. Naturals: 1 = crit success, 12 = crit fail.

Imports nothing from ``combat/`` or ``application/``.

Circumstance modifiers on the die clamp to **±3**. **Advantage** = 2d12 keep **lower**; **disadvantage** = 2d12 keep **higher** — at most one tier; opposing sources cancel.

Everything is a d12 roll-under; old authored difficulty numbers are converted to a die modifier at roll time.

Every d12: natural **1** = critical success, natural **12** = critical failure. **Sharpshooter** / **Swordplay**: a **2** also crits on ranged/thrown and finesse melee attacks.

_Source: `d12_core.py`, `d12_feat_crit.py`._

rows.body_md:
# Advantage and disadvantage

Stacking advantage and disadvantage on d12 rolls.

Each +1 or −1 adds another d12 in that direction: net −2 is three dice, keep
lowest; net +2 is three dice, keep highest. Opposing sources sum (one of each
is a flat roll).

On the phone, **AI Favour** on a roll counts as advantage for that check.

You can hold at most **1** favour token at a time. Net swing is clamped to **±5** in the d12 roller.

## Champion rules (d12)

With Champion rules on, advantage and disadvantage use **d12**: roll **2d12**, keep **lower** (advantage) or **higher** (disadvantage). Only one adv/dis tier applies — they cancel out. AI Favour still counts as advantage for that roll.

_Source: `swing.py`, `d12_core.roll_advantage_d12`, `party/model.py`._

# Skills on actions

Ranked champion skills — catalog + per-PC ranks from abilities YAML.

Every skill starts at level 0 when acquired. Growth is +1 at most per

If the check is an **obstacle** or other world interaction, spending **AI Favour** on that roll also gives advantage.

Authored cooldown tags on skills: `none`, `1/fight`, `1/day`. A session that runs past midnight still counts as one night for growth (**12**-hour rollover).

rows.title: Rest & camp
rows.body_md:
# Rest and camp

Rest: heal, clear conditions, refill pools — and whether the night was quiet.

**Solo rest** (player app, safe room): eat **2 rations** from your pack (any food counts — jerky, bread, cooking ingredients; rations go first, your best ingredients last), get a full recovery pass, pick **downtime**, then sleep **10 minutes** (timed out of travel and other actions). Combat in your room wakes you — benefits already applied. DM can **Wake now** on the PC sheet.

Party **rest** (DM camp intent only) still runs a full recovery pass for everyone:

- Heal **Xd6** where **X** is your level (minimum 1).
- Clear up to **CON mod** condition units (minimum **1**); afflictions left-to-right unless you pick.
- Clear per-rest ability uses.

Then a **d6** decides how quiet the night was (`roll_rest_interruption`):

| d6 | Band | What it means |
|----|------|----------------|
| 1–2 | encounter | Hostile interruption — table runs the fight; CON roll-under saves per PC are surfaced as text, not auto-rolled |
| 3–4 | omen | Flavour omen only |
| 5–6 | clean | Everyone wakes **Bolstered** (+ temp HP, about an hour) |

## Champion rest (d12)

When Champion rules are on, solo and party rest run the d12 pass instead of the table above:

- Heal **d12 hearts** and restore **+1 stamina** (to your cap, default **3** / max **3**).
- Then pick **one**: heal **2d12** hearts instead, gain **+2 stamina**, clear **one status**, or **recharge** one expended spell.

_Source: `party/rest.py`, `party/d12_rest.py`._

rows.title: Down at 0 HP
rows.body_md:
# Down at 0 HP / hearts

## Legacy (hearts HP)

Down and dying: the death timer and the turn-start check_roll.

A PC at 0 HP keeps a seat but does not act. Dropping starts a death timer of
``d4 + CON mod`` (minimum 1). Each time their seat comes up they roll a natural:
a natural 20 stands them up at 1 HP to take that turn; a natural 1 is death;
other rolls tick the timer down, and when it hits 0 they go **stable** (out
cold at 0 HP) instead of dying automatically. Healed to 1+ HP by anyone, the
timer simply stops.

**First aid** (when the table allows it) uses an INT roll to stop the death clock and bring someone to **1 HP**.

## Champion rules (hearts)

At **0 hearts** your seat still ticks, but instead of death saves you make a **WIL** roll-under on your turn: **success** lets you **hang on** and keep acting at 0 hearts; **fail** = **K.O.** If damage would take you far below 0, automatic K.O. rules apply in the app. Healing any positive hearts clears hang-on.

_Source: `combat/dying.py`._

rows.title: Fleeing combat
rows.body_md:
# Escape and fleeing a fight

## Champion Escape (d12)

On the battle map, **Escape** is on the Far band. You need **Near or Far** from every monster — if any monster is **Close**, step back first (the button shows why it is greyed out). Pick an exit, then roll **AGL roll-under** to leave the fight; fail and you stay in combat. If you are **Far from every monster**, the AGL roll has **advantage**.

## Party Escape (legacy vote)

When a **retreat** vote passes (still stored as `retreat` in saves), combat ends and the app rolls the house **d10 Escape table** **2** times (panic on a 9 can chain).

| d10 | Result | Effect |
|-----|--------|--------|
| 1 | Stumble | A champion takes 1d4 damage. |
| 2 | Dropped gear | Something falls on the floor here. |
| 3 | Spilled coin | A champion loses 1d10 Blue Zin. |
| 4 | Torn pack | Another item hits the dirt. |
| 5 | Spilled purse | A champion loses 2d10 Blue Zin. |
| 6 | Shaken | Someone is Distracted fleeing. |
| 7 | Prone | Someone lands wrong — Prone. |
| 8 | Lost supplies | Something from a pack is left behind. |
| 9 | Panic | Roll the table one more time. |
| 10 | Clean break | No extra cost this roll. |

**Surrender** (party vote during combat) ends the fight with **no d10 retreat table**; everyone is **Restrained** and the table moves to the hostile faction's HQ room when the data has one.

**Solo flee** (one champion bailing out on their own) is a CON check with its own d8 fallout table — see **Solo flee**.

_Source: `combat/retreat.py`, `retreat_flee.py`, `combat_surrender.py`._

rows.title: Bonds
rows.body_md:
# Bonds between champions

Propose a bond from **Info → Bonds** or **Me**; NPC bonds in your room can seal when the fiction allows. It starts once the other side accepts.
You can hold **2** active bonds at a time. Each bond type gives one
big upside and one sting — the **Me** tab previews what is live for you right now.

Breaking a bond costs **-1 INT** for **1** session(s).

## Betrothed

_Stand together — guard each other, rise when the other falls._

- **Buff** +2 AC while within Near of your partner
- **Buff** Advantage on fear saves within Near
- **Buff** Once per scene: advantage on one check or save within Near
- **Penalty** Bond-frenzied until end of your next turn when your partner drops to 0 HP

## Lovers

_Heat in the fray — strike harder together, sting when jealousy flares._

- **Buff** +1 attack damage while within Near of your partner
- **Buff** Advantage on your first CHA check each fight while close
- **Buff** Help your lover — they gain Inspired for one round
- **Penalty** Distracted (−2 INT) for 1 round when your lover takes damage from another champion

## Ex-lovers

_The grudge still bites — aim at whoever wronged them, not each other._

- **Buff** +2 on your first attack or check each fight vs whoever last hurt your ex
- **Penalty** −2 CHA with NPCs when your ex is in the scene
- **Penalty** Cannot benefit from Help from your ex

## Parent & child

_A parent's shield and a child's shelter — keep close, bleed for each other._

- **Buff** Once per round, take up to 3 damage meant for your child instead (parent)
- **Buff** +2 on checks within Near of your child
- **Penalty** −2 DEX checks while your child is at 0 HP
- **Other side buff** +2 on checks within Near of your parent
- **Other side buff** Healing you receive is +25% while parent is within Near
- **Other side buff** Once per round, parent may take up to 3 damage for you
- **Other side penalty** −2 on planning (INT) checks when more than Near apart

## Siblings

_Shared scrapes — split the pain, steal each other's luck._

- **Buff** Once per round, redirect up to half the damage you take to your sibling

rows.title: Combat house rules
rows.body_md:
# Combat — house rules in the app

These are enforced by the combat engine and phone API, not optional table chatter. See **[Champion rules (d12)](d12-champions)** when the campaign flag is on.

## Champion combat (d12)

When Champion rules are enabled:

### Vitals and defence

- **Hearts** replace HP — **max hearts = 10 + VIT** (heartstones add permanently).
- Foes expose **armour rating** instead of an attack target number; damage subtracts AR, then hearts.
- Champions roll to **hit** (STR/AGL/PER); **monsters roll damage only** after picking a target.

### Initiative and turns

- **d12** roll-under — **lowest** result goes first. Ambush grants advantage on that roll; being ambushed grants disadvantage.
- **One action** per turn plus **one reaction** per round (dodge/parry below). Weapon swaps inside the **equipped pool** (three slots) are **free**; pulling from the backpack costs your action.

### Attacks, crits, fumbles

- **Melee** `roll_under(STR)` (or AGL on finesse); **ranged** uses **PER** at close/near/far (disadvantage at **close** when ranged).
- **Nat 1** on the attack d12 = **critical hit** → double damage (**champions only**; monsters never crit).
- **Nat 12** on the attack d12 = critical failure — weapon durability and fumble paths in the app (AGL save where authored).
- **Unarmed** defaults to **d2 + STR** in the UI copy; d4 when STR is high enough in data.

### Reactions

When a monster's damage is on the table, the target champion may **dodge** (AGL roll-under) or **parry** (STR roll-under with melee weapon or shield; shield allows parrying ranged). **Success** negates the hit (hearts refund). You choose **after** seeing the damage roll.

### Distance

Combat uses **Close / Near / Far** lanes (close → near → far). Disengage from melee may require an **AGL** check when rules are on.

### Stamina and spells

Spend stamina (default cap **3**) for advantage, feats, scrolls, or recasting expendable spells — see the Me tab.

---

## Legacy combat (pre-d12 flag off)

### Distance

Combat uses **Close / Near / Far** lanes (close → near → far). Default PCs start **near**; hostiles usually **close**. Weapon reach is **melee**, **thrown** (near), or **ranged** (far).

### Round clock

No round limit — a fight runs until every hostile is down or the party retreats.

### Crits and fumbles

- **Champion nat 1 on an attack:** critical hit — double the damage (never spells).
- **Monsters and NPCs never crit.**
- **Nat 1 on attack:** automatic DEX roll or the weapon is destroyed. Guns, power tools and firebombs break with no save.
- **Weapon feats:** do something wild with a weapon (a boss kill, a natural 20, a big hit) to unlock its signature move. It fires once per fight, only while you hold that weapon.
- **Armour:** anyone can wear any armour. Some suits push back instead: a **STR minimum** (below it, attacks and checks roll at disadvantage), **clumsy** (DEX checks and ranged attacks at disadvantage), or extra slots. Some soak a damage kind on top of armour (kevlar vs piercing, boiler plate vs fire).
- **Armour feats:** take a beating in a suit (or the right kind of hit) to unlock its power. It fires once per fight, only while you wear it.

### Morale

Foe morale: one check when the hostile side is down to half its hit points.

The pool is every hostile's max HP this fight, the fallen included, so one
rule covers both shapes of fight — a lone boss checks at half its HP, a swarm
of one-HP goblins checks when half of them are down, and a boss with minions
weighs mostly on the boss. Checked once a fight: the strongest hostile
(highest to-hit, then biggest) rolls d12 + to-hit against DC 12. A fail
breaks them; the DM picks pursue (fight on) or let them flee.

Morale is a roll against **12** in code.

### Backstab

Thieves (classes: shadow, thief) and ledger talents get **+2** weapon dice on a **round-one** swing against a foe that has **not acted yet** and acts after you in initiative.

_Source: `combat/dice.py`, `combat/reactions.py`, `combat/morale.py`, `combat/models.py`, `combat/rails.py`, `combat/backstab.py`, `d12_core.py`._

rows.title: Phone combat
rows.body_md:
# Combat on the phone

When a fight starts the player app switches **in place** to combat pages: an **initiative**
strip, the **battle map**, and a colour-coded combat log. Swipe between the info and actions pages.

## Joining

Only champions **in the fight's room** get an initiative seat. If you walk in mid-fight, tap
**Join combat** in the room's side column.

## Stepping into a new fight

If **travel**, **gather**, or a **go-to** target would put you in a room where idle hostiles would
start combat as soon as you arrive, the app shows a **bottom-sheet confirm** — say **Yes** or stay
put. **Go hostile** on someone already in your room still starts a fight at once (no travel sheet).

## On your turn

- Tap a foe (card or map token) to open its **action menu**: attack, cast, skill, or use an item.
- You may use **one optional skill** first; attack, cast and item use each **end your turn**.
- **End turn** passes without acting. If you go quiet for **60 seconds**,
  your turn passes automatically.
- No weapon? Fists hit for **d2 + STR**.

## Bosses telegraph

Bosses announce **who they are swinging at next**. Some items and skills can pull that
attention onto someone else — or clear it.

## When it ends

When the last foe drops you get a **kill-or-KO** choice for anyone left down; it stays up
until you answer. Running away on your own is **Solo flee**; the whole party leaving is a
**retreat** vote.

## Champion rules on the phone

When Champion rules are enabled:

- Header shows **hearts** and **stamina** pips; the equipped **pool** (three slots) replaces pack quick slots for combat-ready gear.
- After hostile damage, a **dodge / parry** banner may appear — one reaction per round for that champion.
- Rolls and the combat log show **d12 roll-under** detail (ability score vs die, nat 1/12 callouts).
- Initiative strip marks **low first** seating.

## What you do not see

Exact foe HP or hearts (health bands only), DM tactics, hidden mechanics. Turn gating is enforced
**server-side** — greyed buttons are not hints. Full-cover targets show **No shot**.

_Source: player combat API, `combat/reactions.py`, `away.py`, `boss_targeting.py`._

rows.body_md:
# Supplies, statuses, and loot

Table conventions the app enforces on your phone — not optional house chatter.

## Ammunition

Ranged ammo stacks **20 shots per inventory slot**. Each shot with the matching weapon spends one
round; weight drops with the count. Empty means you cannot fire until you buy or find more.

## Bleeding and debuffs

Most short debuffs and many buffs last about **20 minutes** of real time unless the scene says
otherwise. **Bleeding** lasts about **20 minutes**: dis STR and AGL; legacy bleed ticks 1 HP / 10 min. Stat drain chips (Clumsy, Feeble,
and the rest) clear on the same clock. Long-press a status chip to see what caused it.

## Meat and the Champion Cooler

**Meat**, **flesh**, and other `Meat` cooking tags in your pack spoil after about **90 minutes**
unless you carry a **Champion Cooler** (or Second Helping Cooler). Spoiled meat drops from the pack
when the timer fires.

## Failed searches

**6 failed** secret flips or room searches **in one room** (party-wide, not
consecutive) trigger a **wander encounter** in that room; the counter then resets. Everyone gets a
line when it happens.

## Corpse loot

Regular monster corpses (not bosses): **50%** bronze-tier pocket change **or** **50%** one
**Bronze Loot Box** — never both. Bosses and special kills use the tier tables in **Loot boxes**.

## Class feats (champion)

Champions have **no character levels or XP**. Each **4 party hope** (4, 8, 12, …) earns **one class feat pick**
on the Me tab. **Second way** (once): take a second class and a feat from its list — no third class, no kit.
Training feats are repeatable. New PCs spend a **56-point** stat screen (eight stats **5–9**, at most one **9**); max hearts = **10 + VIT**.

_Source: `hope_feats.py`, `feat_pick.py`, `stat_pick.py`, `level_up.py`._

# Floor 3 — table conventions

Rival kitchens: who the party has made an enemy of, and who it cooks against next.

The loop is endless: hunt the jungle, cook at the Stadium, win into the Library,
back to the jungle. Each service draws one opponent. A rival is drawn at random
from the party's rivals (never the same one twice running when there's a
choice) with a score frozen from its authored range and whichever of its tricks
fire. No rivals at all and the party cooks the house show instead: a par that
rises every time they beat it.

The draw is announced before ingredients are committed and is held until the
service is submitted, so reopening the panel never rerolls it.

Everything here lasts one game night. A new evening (session start, or the
party calling it a night) means a new table: no rivals, the house par back to
its start, and only tonight's deeds can make new ones.

**Archive** on the phone lists rooms, people, and gear only after the party has **discovered** them in play — same boundary as this handbook's discovered sections.

# Classes

Legacy nights: level 1 picks your class; HP is the class hit die plus CON. Champion rules: pick class on the Me tab, starting kit gear, then class feats from party hope — max hearts **10 + VIT**, stats are plain numbers (no modifiers).

## Blade

Hold the line; cleave, parry, and favoured steel.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Strike — at will. Close melee 1d8 using STR.
- **Major** Guard — spend 1 stamina to parry without using your reaction when Bastion allows.

## Magic

Arcane study, battle magic, and prepared power.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Cantrip spark — at will. Close arcane poke 1d4 using KNO.
- **Major** Study — advantage on KNO to recall lore about magic and traps.
- **Minor** Focus — spend 1 stamina to cast a known spell as a free action once per scene.

## Light

Blessings, light, and steadfast spirits.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Rebuke — at will. Near blessing spark 1d6 light using CHA.
- **Major** Comfort — advantage on CHA to befriend or calm the frightened.

## Wild

Track, shoot, and endure the wild.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Shot — at will. Ranged or thrown 1d8 using PER.
- **Major** Track — advantage on PER to follow tracks and forage.

## Shadow

Sneak, stab, and slip away.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Nimble cut — at will. Close small melee 1d6 using AGL.
- **Major** Hide — advantage on STE to hide in combat.
- **Minor** Light fingers — advantage on pick pockets and traps.

## Song

Song, silver tongue, and battlefield tempo.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Finesse strike — at will. Close finesse melee 1d8 using CHA.
- **Major** Battle hum — once per scene, an ally within near gains +1 damage this fight.
- **Minor** Encore — perform for a room once per rest without a roll.

_Source: `dungeons/global/classes.yaml`._

rows.body_md:
# Races

Race picks open at levels 2, 6, 9; a later pick swaps the old one.

## Huma

The most widespread Kin. Humas are extremely versatile, and can be recognized by their pointy ears.

- **Major** Versatility — repeat your last failed ability roll. Button on the sheet; refreshes on a short rest. (+1 reroll_failed_once_per_rest)

## Kedi

Standing at about half the height of a huma, kedis are agile and nimble catfolk hailing from the desert.

- **Major** Night eyes — see in darkness without a torch. (+1 night_vision)
- **Minor** Nimble — +1 on dodge rolls; +1 on rolls to reduce fall damage. (+1 dodge_bonus, +1 fall_no_damage)

## Pengu

The tallest snow-capped peaks are home to the pengus, penguin-people gifted with extraordinary physical resistance.

- **Major** Thick skin — +3 hearts. Your feathers let you endure COLD 1. (+3 extra_hearts)
- **Minor** Endure cold 1 — bitter air does not bite as hard. (+1 endure_cold)

## Strix

There are strixen of all shapes and sizes, but all of them have round dark heads, shiny eyes, and a natural talent for magic.

- **Major** Innate magic — know 2 arcane spells of your choice. (+2 arcane_spells_pick)
- **Minor** Night eyes — see in the dark without a torch. (+1 night_vision)

## Toluna

The horned toluna hail from the coast and boast striking muscles and innate physical prowess.

- **Major** Physical prowess — +1 stamina. (+1 extra_stamina)
- **Minor** Endure hot 1 — scorching air is home ground. (+1 endure_hot)

_Source: `dungeons/global/races.yaml`._
